To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CM energy in the collision of charged particles near the horizon of rotating black holes in an electromagnetic field is arbitrarily large when a charged particle plunging from the ISCO and another particle colliding with the first particle near the horizon are both charged and the magnetic field is sufficiently strong.

the center-of-mass energy of charged particle collisions near a rotating black hole can be made arbitrarily large as the black hole approaches maximal rotation under a condition that a charged particle falls from the innermost circular stable orbit and collides with a particle near the horizon, while a particle orbiting the innermost stable orbit around a spinning blackhole needs arbitrarily high energy for the strong magnetic field limit.

the center-of-mass energy can be arbitrarily increased as the uniformly magnetizing black hole arbitrarily approaches the maximal rotation, under the situation that one particle plunges from a stable circular orbit and collides with the other particle near the horizon, and that the charged particle needs an arbitrarily high energy to orbit the ISCO in the strong field regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility that a rotating black hole can be a powerful particle accelerator in the weak magnetic field limit.
the possibility of the acceleration of charged particles by a rotating black hole in the weak field limit.
the effect of a weak electromagnetic field on particle acceleration by a rotating black hole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CM energy is bounded from above by the energy of the particle plunging from the ISCO, and the magnetic field may substantially promote the CM energy in the weak field limit.
the CM energy is arbitrarily large if a rotating black hole is magnetized and approaches maximal rotation in the limit of the weak magnetic field.

the CM energy of colliding particles near the horizon of the uniformly magnetized spinning black hole can be arbitrarily large, when the magnetic field is weak enough and the black hole rotates sufficiently rapidly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CM energy is maximized by the fine-tuning of the magnetic field, the black hole spin, and the energy of a particle orbiting the black hole.

, for a rotating black hole, the fine-tuning is not required for the arbitrarily large CM energy in the weak magnetic field, while the strong magnetic field is required for the arbitrarily high energy of the charged particle orbitting near the ISCO.

a charged particle colliding with a particle orbiting the innermost stable orbit around a rotating black holes can be a good particle accelerator in astrophysics, if the magnetic field and the black hole spin are not too strong.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CM energy in a weak electromagnetic field is limited by the spin of the black hole.
the CM energy is not only sensitive to the black hole spin, but also depends on the particle energy.
the CM energy in the vicinity of the rotating black hole can be arbitrarily large if the magnetic field around the black hole is sufficiently strong.
